--- title: "Methods & Benchmarks" description: "Every model in uncertainty_flow, when to use it, how they compare, and how to run your own benchmarks" date: today format: html: self-contained: true embed-resources: true code-fold: true code-tools: true --- # Methods & Benchmarks This notebook is a **model selection guide** backed by benchmark data. 1. **Model Reference** — every model, its method, coverage guarantee, and use case 2. **Key Findings** — data-driven insights from real benchmarks 3. **Running Benchmarks** — Python API and CLI 4. **Visual Comparison** — coverage vs sharpness across datasets ## Model Reference | Model | Method | Coverage | Speed | Best For | |-------|--------|----------|-------|----------| | `ConformalRegressor` | Split conformal | Guaranteed (finite-sample) | Fast | Tabular regression, new users | | `ConformalForecaster` | Conformal + time features | Guaranteed (exchangeable) | Fast | Time series, any sklearn regressor | | `QuantileForestForecaster` | Quantile regression forest | Empirical | Medium | Sharp intervals, feature importance | | `DeepQuantileNet` | sklearn MLP quantile net | Empirical | Medium | Nonlinear patterns, no conformal | | `ConformalClassifier` | APS (Romano et al. 2020) | Guaranteed | Fast | Multi-class classification | | `AdaptiveConformalForecaster` | Gibbs & Candes ACI | Adaptive | Fast | Streaming / distribution shift | | `EnsembleBootstrapPI` | EnbPI (Xu & Xie 2021) | Empirical | Slow | Time series ensemble | | `ConformalRiskControl` | Risk-controlled conformal | On risk metric | Fast | Cost-sensitive decisions | ## Benchmark Findings ::: {#setup .cell cache='true' execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt ``` ::: ::: {#load-data .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw = pl.read_csv("../docs/benchmarks/comparison_table.csv", try_parse_dates=False) print(f"Datasets: {raw['dataset'].unique().to_list()}") print(f"Models: {raw['model'].unique().to_list()}") print(f"Total rows: {len(raw)}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Datasets: ['electricity', 'weather', 'exchange_rate'] Models: ['bayesian-quantile', 'ridge-regression', 'moving-average', 'deep-quantile', 'naive-forecast', 'conformal-forecaster', 'random-forest', 'linear-regression', 'quantile-forest', 'conformal-regressor', 'deep-quantile-torch', 'gradient-boosting'] Total rows: 36 ``` ::: ::: ### Finding 1: Coverage-Accuracy Tradeoff ::: {#cell-coverage-table .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} summary = raw.group_by("model").agg([ pl.col("coverage_90").mean().alias("mean_coverage_90"), pl.col("winkler_90").mean().alias("mean_winkler_90"), pl.col("crps").mean().alias("mean_crps"), pl.col("mae").mean().alias("mean_mae"), pl.col("train_time_sec").mean().alias("mean_train_time"), ]).sort("mean_coverage_90", descending=True) summary ``` ::: {#coverage-table .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Finding 2: Coverage vs Sharpness by Dataset ::: {#cell-scatter-grid .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} datasets = raw["dataset"].unique().to_list() n_ds = len(datasets) fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, n_ds, figsize=(5 * n_ds, 5), sharey=True) if n_ds == 1: axes = [axes] markers = {"conformal-regressor": "o", "conformal-forecaster": "s", "quantile-forest": "^", "deep-quantile": "D"} colors_map = {"conformal-regressor": "#4C78A8", "conformal-forecaster": "#F58518", "quantile-forest": "#54A24B", "deep-quantile": "#E45756"} for ax, ds in zip(axes, datasets): subset = raw.filter(pl.col("dataset") == ds) for row in subset.iter_rows(named=True): m = row["model"] ax.scatter( row["coverage_90"], row["winkler_90"], marker=markers.get(m, "o"), c=colors_map.get(m, "gray"), s=100, label=m if ds == datasets[0] else None, edgecolors="black", linewidth=0.5, ) ax.axvline(x=0.9, color="gray", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5) ax.set_xlabel("Coverage (90%)") ax.set_title(ds) axes[0].set_ylabel("Winkler score (90%)") axes[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left") plt.suptitle("Coverage vs Sharpness — Lower-Left is Better", fontsize=13) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](05_benchmarks_files/figure-html/scatter-grid-output-1.png){#scatter-grid width=1428 height=475} ::: ::: ### Finding 3: Model Rankings ::: {#cell-rankings .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} ranked = summary.with_columns([ pl.col("mean_winkler_90").rank().alias("winkler_rank"), pl.col("mean_crps").rank().alias("crps_rank"), pl.col("mean_coverage_90").rank(descending=True).alias("coverage_rank"), ]).select(["model", "coverage_rank", "winkler_rank", "crps_rank"]) ranked ``` ::: {#rankings .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

Running Your Own Benchmarks ### Python API ::: {#python-api .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} from uncertainty_flow.benchmarking import BenchmarkRunner, BenchmarkConfig from uncertainty_flow import ConformalRegressor, QuantileForestForecaster from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingRegressor config = BenchmarkConfig( models={ "conformal-gb": lambda: ConformalRegressor( base_model=GradientBoostingRegressor(random_state=42), ), "qrf": lambda: QuantileForestForecaster(random_state=42), }, datasets=["weather", "electricity"], n_obs=1000, horizon=3, ) runner = BenchmarkRunner(config) results = runner.run() results.save("my_benchmark.json") ``` ::: ### CLI ```{bash} #| label: cli-examples #| eval: false uf benchmark --models conformal-regressor quantile-forest --datasets weather electricity --n-obs 1000 uf compare --files benchmark_run1.json benchmark_run2.json uf list-datasets uf auto-tune --model quantile-forest --dataset weather ``` ## Recommendations | Scenario | Recommended Model | Why | |----------|-------------------|-----| | First time, tabular data | `ConformalRegressor` | Guaranteed coverage, simple API | | Time series, stationary | `ConformalForecaster` | Temporal awareness, guaranteed coverage | | Time series, distribution shift | `AdaptiveConformalForecaster` | ACI adapts intervals automatically | | Need sharpest intervals | `QuantileForestForecaster` | Native quantile predictions, empirically sharp | | Cost-sensitive decisions | `ConformalRiskControl` | Optimizes for your cost function, not just coverage | | Multi-class classification | `ConformalClassifier` | APS prediction sets with guaranteed coverage | | High-dimensional / complex | `DeepQuantileNet` | MLP can capture nonlinear patterns | ## Key Takeaways - **Start with `ConformalRegressor`** — guaranteed coverage with any sklearn model - **Benchmark on your own data** — results vary by dataset; no single best model - **Use `BenchmarkRunner`** for systematic comparison across models and datasets - **Coverage ≠ quality** — also look at Winkler score (sharpness) and CRPS
